prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the continuous ground plane of the wide asphalt road and curbed sidewalk stretching from ~1–2 m at the bottom foreground to over 25 m on the right, while isolating the line of palm trees and median islands at ~8–25 m across all five frames. As the camera wearer turns left in frame 2 and then pans back right in frames 3–5, the map reveals a foreground counter on the lower left (~1–1.5 m away, just within or near the camera wearer's arm's reach) occluding the lower bodies of two people standing ~0.5 m apart under a canopy tent (~3–4 m away, facing roughly toward the camera wearer with the counter within their arm's reach), a tripod speaker (~2–3 m away) to their right, a blue car (~4–5 m) behind the people, and a white car (~8–10 m) behind the speaker. In frames 3 and 4, the tent and people pass out of view on the left while the speaker (~2–3 m) and white car (~8–10 m, partially cropped at the left edge of frame 4) recede to the left as the view opens back onto the road. Compared to the sun-glared RGB image in frame 2, the depth map much more clearly separates the near occluding counter and speaker stand from the mid-ground canopy and background trees. However, the map is unreliable in merging the two people and the blue car behind them into flat, indistinct mid-grey silhouettes that lack head orientation or gaze detail, and it loses distant cars and pedestrians beyond ~20–30 m into uniform dark grey or black.
descriptions.segmentation: Across the five-frame pan from the palm-lined roadway on the right (frame 1) to the roadside canopy setup on the left (frame 2) and back to the open road (frames 3–5), the segmentation map leaves the background layout mostly unlabelled black and highlights only discrete foreground and mid-ground objects. In frame 2, it segments the two people standing side-by-side (~0.5 m apart, ~3–4 m from the camera wearer, facing toward the camera with the unlabelled ~1–1.5 m foreground counter occluding their lower bodies and within their arm's reach), placing them in front of the blue car (~4–5 m away) and to the left of both the tripod speaker (~2–3 m away) and the white car (~8–10 m away) beneath the overhead canopy. As the camera turns right across frames 3 to 5, the people and tent exit the left edge, leaving only a small mask at the bottom left of frame 3 (~1.5–2 m away, near the camera wearer's reach), the partly cropped white car at the far left edge of frame 4 (~8–10 m away), and a distant white car on the far right of frame 5 (~30+ m away). The instance masks in frame 2 help separate the overlapping boundaries of the two people from the blue car right behind them despite the heavy RGB lens flare. However, the map is highly unreliable in its class labels and coverage: it misclassifies the overhead canopy and light pole as an 'airplane', the tripod speaker as a 'traffic light', and the ground box in frame 3 as a 'car', while completely missing the foreground occluding counter, all trees, and distant pedestrians.
descriptions.pose: Because the pose map is completely black across all five frames with zero detected body or hand skeletons, all spatial understanding of the scene's people and layout must be drawn from the RGB strip. In the RGB context, the camera wearer stands by a curbed road lined with palm trees (~8–25 m away on the right) and pans left in frame 2 to view two people standing ~0.5 m apart under a canopy tent (~3–4 m away) in front of a blue car (~4–5 m away) and to the left of a tripod speaker (~2–3 m away) and white car (~8–10 m away), before panning right across frames 3–5 as those people and objects move out of view on the left. In frame 2, both people stand behind a dark foreground counter (~1–1.5 m from the camera wearer, near the edge of the camera wearer's reach) that occludes their lower bodies, facing and looking generally toward the camera wearer with their arms lowered within reach of the counter surface in front of them. Distant figures near the median crosswalk (~20–30 m away) in frames 1, 3, and 4 are also present along the roadway to the right of the tent setup. The pose map contributes nothing beyond the RGB image and is completely unreliable here, failing to detect the two people in frame 2 due to strong backlighting, lower-body occlusion behind the counter, and ~3–4 m distance, as well as missing the tiny pedestrians in the far background.
